draft.title: Foreshadowing
card: Foreshadowing is a hint early in a story about something that will happen later. The writer plants it before the reader knows it matters.
A hint can be an object, a line of dialogue, a setting detail or a mood. For example: "The old bridge groaned as Tai crossed it." This may hint that the bridge will fail later.
Foreshadowing builds suspense, because the reader senses that something is coming and wants to find out what.
It also makes the ending feel earned. When the event arrives, the reader can look back and see the hints that led to it.
draft.remember: Foreshadowing plants an early hint of a later event, so readers feel suspense and the outcome feels earned.

a.q: Early in a story, Priya notices a crack spreading across the ice of the lake. Later the ice breaks under her brother. What is the crack an example of?
opts: Foreshadowing, a hint of a later event
Flashback, a return to an earlier event
Setting, which is only a place description
a.why: The crack is planted before the ice breaks, so it hints at what will happen later. That is foreshadowing. It is not a flashback, because the story does not go back in time.
a.clue: Does the detail point forward or backward in the story?

b.q: In chapter one, Mr Boyd locks a small box in his desk and tells Ellie never to touch it. In the last chapter, Ellie opens the box and finds the letter that solves the mystery. What is the main effect of the first scene?
opts: It makes the ending feel earned, as the box was set up
It shows the reader events from Mr Boyd's past
It tells the reader the ending before it happens
It gives the reader a full description of the box
b.why: The box is introduced early, so the later discovery feels planned rather than random. The first scene does not reveal the ending, and it does not go back to the past. It only hints that the box will matter.
b.clue: Think about how the reader feels when the box returns in the last chapter.

a.best: Foreshadowing, a hint of a later event

b.best: It makes the ending feel earned, as the box was set up
